SLA Language Reference > Functions and Control Flow

Functions and Control Flow

This page explains how to write fn, methods and associated functions, closures, and if/else, while, for in, break/continue, and ? error propagation. After reading this page, you can write structurally complete SLA functions that pass sa sla check.

Function declarations

Functions are declared with fn; parameters carry type annotations, and the return value follows ->. Bindings are mutable by default; const is for immutable bindings. Visibility is marked with pub (demos/rosetta/42_export_visibility/main.sla):

pub fn exported_value() -> i32 {
    7
}

fn internal_value() -> i32 {
    5
}

Function overloading (multiple signatures under one name)

Both ordinary functions and extern declarations support multiple signatures under one name: at registration time they are renamed by parameter signature, with member keys of the form <name>__ov_<tag> (the tag encodes the parameter types); a singleton forms no set and keeps the old symbol. The matching discipline is exact matching after inference: the argument types are inferred first, and a call is allowed only when exactly one candidate matches; no match or ambiguity (AmbiguousCall) errors loudly; overloading by return value alone is forbidden. The real form (from tests/test_unit_overload_variadic_arity.sla):

fn vsum(code: i32, extra: i32) -> i64 { return 1000 + (code + extra) as i64; }
extern "C" fn vsum(tag: ptr, args: ...) -> i64 { let a = va_next_i32(args); return a as i64; }

// 按实参类型选中对应成员
let r = vsum(1, 2);       // 命中 i32/i32 定元成员
let r2 = unsafe { vsum(tag_ptr, 7) };  // 命中 ptr/变参成员
NoteGeneric/overload combinations (GenericOverloadConflict), and duplicate method names in an impl, are all loudly rejected; taking an overload set name bare as a function value reports AmbiguousCall (member symbols can be referenced directly). This capability landed on 2026-10-30 (sa_plugin_sla).

extern variadics (C-style ...)

Only the extern "C" surface supports variadic parameters; writing ... in an ordinary fn, a closure, or a non-C-ABI fn type is loudly rejected in all cases. ... must be trailing and must be preceded by at least one fixed parameter. Declaration / call forms (tests/test_unit_variadic_extern_call.sla):

extern "C" {
    fn sprintf(buf: ptr, fmt: ptr, ...) -> i32;
}
let n = unsafe { sprintf(buf, STR_PTR("%u:%lld\0"), byte_val, -5000000000) };

When defining a variadic function for C callers, use an args: ... (VaList) parameter and read in order through the typed va_next_i32 / i64 / u32 / u64 / f64 / ptr builtins (tests/test_unit_variadic_define.sla):

extern "C" fn va_sum3(fixed: i32, args: ...) -> i64 {
    let a = va_next_i32(args);
    let b = va_next_i32(args);
    return fixed as i64 + a as i64 + b as i64;
}
NoteCall sites follow the C default argument promotions (integers narrower than i32 are promoted to i32/u32, f32 to f64); only scalars and raw pointers may pass; aggregates / String / Vec handles / borrows are all loudly rejected. The C / wasm / JS targets loudly reject variadics (UnsupportedVariadic), and the interpreted path traps with RunError.UnsupportedVariadic; the variadic definition surface currently supports only x86_64 SysV. The read order is the caller's protocol responsibility — it must correspond one by one with the types the callee actually reads. This capability landed on 2026-10-31 (sa_plugin_sla + sci).

Methods, self, and impl blocks

In impl 类型 { ... }, a method's first parameter is written self or &self, and calls use method syntax (UFCS static expansion). The following is from demos/rosetta/40_impl_block_state/main.sla and demo 311:

impl Account {
    fn deposit(self, amount: i32) -> Account {
        return Account { balance: self.balance + amount };
    }
}

// 调用
let updated = account.deposit(5);

impl Meter {
    fn double(self) -> i32 { return self.value.double(); }
}

Closures

Closure literals are written |参数| 表达式 and can capture outer local values (demos/rosetta/08_closures/main.sla):

let offset = 5;
let add_offset = |x: i32| x + offset;
let result = add_offset(10);   // 15

if / else expressions

if/else produces a value and can be used directly as a function body's tail expression or for field initialization (demos 03_if_else and 45_config_merge):

fn max(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 {
    if a > b { a } else { b }
}

Config {
    threads: if override_cfg.threads == 0 { base.threads } else { override_cfg.threads },
    level: if override_cfg.level == 0 { base.level } else { override_cfg.level },
}

Loops: while / for in / break / continue

while cond { ... } is the basic loop; break/continue can exit early or skip. Numeric range loops for i in start..end are directly supported; for x in collection iteration over collections is still not fully covered on some paths (see the Feature Maturity Matrix page). Real examples:

// demos/rosetta/103_labeled_break/main.sla（while + break）
while done == false {
    inner = inner + 1;
    if inner >= 3 { break; };
}

// rosetta 各 demo 中常见的区间循环
for i in 0..4 {
    total = total + i;
}

? error propagation

? acts on a call returning Result<T, E>: on error it extracts the error and returns early; on success it unwraps T and continues (demos/rosetta/309_try_block_macro/main.sla):

@import "sa_std/core/result.sa"

fn parse_num(value: i32) -> Result<i32, i32> {
    Ok(value)
}

fn compute() -> Result<i32, i32> {
    let a = parse_num(10)?;
    let b = parse_num(20)?;
    Ok(a + b)
}
Notepanic(code) fails immediately and carries an integer diagnostic code; it is the uniform assertion mechanism of all @test demos.

Test blocks

@test "rosetta 012 12_destructuring"() {
    let got = destructured_sum();
    if got != 7 {
        panic(12);
    };
};

Program entry: the main contract

An executable program's entry point is an ordinary function named main: the checker applies no special-casing to main's signature; the contract is enforced by the host layer — the host generates a C entry wrapper only for a function that is "of ordinary-function kind, named main, with 0 parameters". A main with parameters gets no wrapper, i.e. there is no entry point (and currently no diagnostic; loud rejection by the checker is a batch-three candidate). The corpus convention is one-sided: every fn main in tests and demos is fn main() -> i32.

  • Return value and exit code: compiled path — the entry wrapper calls main with zero arguments, and the return value is cast to i32 as the process exit code; a void return is filled with 0; a fallible return takes its status field. Interpreted path — the exit code is main's return value truncated to u8 (fallible likewise takes status, truncated), plus reserved codes: program-set exit (UserExit), division by zero 100, call-stack overflow 108.
  • argv does not go through parameters: the wrapper stores the host's argc / argv into globals; inside the program they are read via the SA layer's sys_argc / sys_argv, or a JSON handle is obtained via the std env domain's @extern sa_env_args_json(). Under wasm_compat the entry name becomes __main_argc_argv (the WASI contract).
  • main must be synchronous: the host layer has no async entry form. Writing async fn main is currently not rejected by the checker, but its future return value is treated by the entry wrapper as an ordinary return value and never driven — the program silently fails rather than erroring loudly (this failure form is inferred from the code path and has not been probe-verified). The convention is that main is a synchronous function, and asynchronous work is driven inside main in std's block_on form (the polling driver in sa_std/async.sla). Loud rejection of async main by the checker is likewise a batch-three candidate.

Related pages: Pattern Matching, async/await: Current State.
